body.title: Send invoice throws TypeError in InvoiceSendButton.tsx on /invoices/new
body.summary: The user filled in a new invoice's customer and amount, saved it as a draft, and then clicked Send invoice. The send action threw a TypeError, the button was rage-clicked, and the invoice was not sent.
body.expected: The invoice is sent without an error.
body.actual: Clicking Send invoice raises TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') at sendInvoice (InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21). The user then rage-clicked the Send invoice button five times.

evidence.note: Primary failure: uncaught TypeError in sendInvoice at InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21 when Send invoice is clicked.
Same TypeError logged to the console at the moment of the send click.
Five rapid clicks on Send invoice show the user was blocked and retried.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that sendInvoice reads an .id property from an undefined object, possibly because the invoice or customer record is not available in the state after the draft save.
body.signature: exc:TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') @ InvoiceSendButton.tsx

body.title: Send reminder fails with 500 (reported by [email])
body.summary: The user opened invoice inv_8812 and clicked Send reminder, which failed. They clicked Send reminder again a few seconds later and got the same error.
body.expected: Clicking Send reminder sends the reminder for the invoice without error.
body.actual: POST /api/invoices/inv_8812/reminders returned 500 (internal_error) and the user saw "Something went wrong. Please try again." on each attempt.

evidence.note: Primary failure: the reminders endpoint returned 500 with internal_error.
The user was shown a generic error message after the failed request.
The retry produced the same 500 from the same endpoint, so the failure is repeatable.
The same generic error message was shown on the retry.

body.suspected_cause: A likely server-side exception in the reminders endpoint for this invoice, since the API returns internal_error on every attempt.

body.title: AR aging report times out with 504 from /api/reports/aging
body.summary: The user opened /reports and clicked AR aging (#aging-report), then rage-clicked the link four times. The aging request returned 504 gateway_timeout after 30012 ms, and the user was shown a message to try a shorter range.
body.expected: The AR aging report loads and displays.
body.actual: The request to /api/reports/aging?range=… returned 504 (gateway_timeout) after 30012 ms, and the user saw "This report is taking too long. Try a shorter range."

evidence.note: The aging report request timed out with a 504 after 30012 ms, which is the primary failure.
The user rage-clicked #aging-report four times, suggesting they were waiting for a response that never came.
The user was shown a timeout message suggesting a shorter range, so the report never displayed.

body.suspected_cause: Likely the aging report query for the default range takes longer than the gateway's 30-second limit, causing the 504.

body.title: Payments page fails to load with ChunkLoadError for chunk 812 after deploy
body.summary: The user opened the dashboard and clicked Payments to open /payments. The page request failed because the JavaScript chunk 812.3f9a1c.chunk.js returned 404, and the user saw "Page failed to load."
body.expected: The Payments page loads and shows the user's payments.
body.actual: The Payments page does not load. A chunk request returns 404 and the user sees "Page failed to load."

evidence.note: Primary failure: GET /static/js/812.3f9a1c.chunk.js returned 404 in 35 ms.
ChunkLoadError for chunk 812 at the same URL confirms the page code could not be loaded.
The user-facing message "Page failed to load." shows the page was blocked for the user.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is a stale client bundle after the 2026.10.27-1 deploy, where the browser references chunk 812 from an older build that is no longer served.

body.body: +1 from another session (Chrome 141, app 2026.10.27-2): POST /api/invoices/inv_7731/pdf -> 500 in 2800 ms (pdf_render_failed) at [00:02]. Replay: https://us.posthog.com/project/102/replay/rec_07_pdf_dup?t=0

body.title: Customers CSV export returns 500 and shows "Export failed." on Export CSV click
body.summary: On the customers page the user clicked Export CSV (#export-csv) to download a CSV. The export request returned a 500 error and the user saw the message "Export failed."

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the customers page at /customers with a search query.

body.expected: The customers CSV export completes and the file downloads.
body.actual: The export request GET /api/customers/export returns 500 (export_failed) in about 920 ms, and the user sees "Export failed."

evidence.note: The export request to /api/customers/export returns 500 with export_failed, which is the primary failure.
The console logs an error for the failed export with a 500 status, confirming the failure is on the export path.
The user is shown the generic "Export failed." message, so the failure is visible to them.

body.suspected_cause: The server-side customers export handler likely throws an unhandled error for this request, possibly tied to the query parameters it receives.

body.title: QuickBooks "Sync now" on /settings/integrations returns 500 and shows a sync failure message
body.summary: On the integrations settings page, the user clicked Sync now for QuickBooks. The request POST /api/integrations/quickbooks/sync returned 500 after 5100 ms, and the user was shown "Sync failed. We'll retry automatically."
body.expected: The QuickBooks sync completes successfully without an error.
body.actual: The sync request fails with a 500 response after about 5 seconds, and the user sees "Sync failed. We'll retry automatically."

evidence.note: The sync POST returns 500 after 5100 ms, which is the primary failure.
The user sees the sync failed message, confirming the failure is visible to them.

body.suspected_cause: A likely server-side error in the QuickBooks sync endpoint, since the request returns 500 with a sync_failed code.

body.title: Revenue report crashes with RangeError after applying a custom date range
body.summary: The user opened the revenue report and set a custom date range on the date picker, typing a start date and clicking Apply. The page then failed with an invalid time value error and showed a generic 'Something went wrong' message, after which the user repeatedly clicked Apply.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Type a value into the start date field.

body.expected: The selected date range is applied and the revenue report loads for that range.
body.actual: The report fails with a RangeError: Invalid time value thrown in formatDateRange, and the user sees 'Something went wrong loading this report.' Repeated clicks on Apply do not recover it.

evidence.note: Primary failure: uncaught RangeError thrown in formatDateRange in DateRangePicker.tsx right after Apply.
Console error confirms the same invalid time value error at the moment of failure.
The user is shown a generic error message, so the report does not load.
Rage clicks on Apply show the user is stuck and retrying without success.

body.suspected_cause: The date picker likely passes an unparseable or empty date value into formatDateRange after the start date is typed, causing an Invalid Date to be formatted.
